key_insight: Interactive video world models can generate objects passing through physical obstacles, even though their internal representations contain information that could predict these violations. NoPeBench exposes this gap between physical awareness and reliable generation.
problem_solved: Evaluating whether interactive video world models respect solid obstacles rather than allowing physically impossible object penetration.
method: Introduce NoPeBench to evaluate how world models respond to physical obstacles.
Test open-source models and find that none reliably prevent object-penetration failures in the reported evaluation.
Analyze internal representations and identify information predictive of penetration violations. The supplied abstract is truncated, so further method details are unavailable.
impact: NoPeBench gives practitioners a way to assess physical consistency beyond visual quality. The findings suggest that internal model signals could help guide future safeguards, although the supplied excerpt does not establish a prevention method.
visual_elements: Side-by-side video frames showing an object stopping at a wall versus passing through it.
Evaluation pipeline: obstacle interaction → generated video → penetration assessment.
Conceptual diagram contrasting internal warning signals with a physically invalid generated outcome.
Benchmark scorecard highlighting the reported lack of reliable penetration prevention, without inventing numerical results.
paper_authors: Yuhang Dai, Yinwei Wu, Ziyue Lin, Han Ji, Xingyi Yang
